title: hiddenone's Feedback Fridays (it's September 2025 & I'm back at it!)

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Need someone to break your game
and
your spirit? Look no further!
​
I love playtesting and have played a ton of demos here on the forum, but finding new options can be tough. So I'm opening up this thread to make it easier for people who need playtesting and feedback to reach out! You can leave a comment in the thread with a link to your game or PM me, and tell me what you'd like me to focus on or if you'd like my general thoughts on everything while playing.
And now for the main reason for this thread, the
Spooky Month Game Jam
feedback! I've kept things pretty short so that I didn't lose my mind completely, but if you have any specific questions please ask and I'll explain my thoughts.
Spoiler
Whispers in the Bitter Frost by
@Starmage
Spoiler
Quite a creepy story as the player realizes what is wrong, though I do wish there was more buildup to the full reveal. I know the jam had a deadline, but it did feel rushed when Avelina and Marcus got their memories back. There wasn't a lot of time for the horror of them being trapped and brainwashed to really sink in, so the ending was missing a bit of 'oomph' to really sell just how much Avelina had lost. I had guessed the doctors were evil along with the lord, but I almost wish they had been normal humans just to make the situation more horrific (instead of being vampire monsters, they were still humans and still sacrificing blood to their god in the hopes of drawing its attention).
The combat and running gameplay worked, but I don't know if it really added to the game. I spammed the attack button without moving and won easily, and I seemed to be fine just zig-zagging in the dark. I found Potions but never had to use them, though I did find that I could destroy them by trying to use them when my HP was full. The music and sound effect choices were pretty good, but the clacking during messages was very distracting so I wish there had been an option to turn it off. Overall, this game suited the jam but I wish the gameplay had either gotten more attention or you had ditched it entirely and focused on the story and spooks.
Psyche by
@TheAM-Dol
Spoiler
An interesting take on the jam, but I don't think a person's mind really counts for a haunted building. I did like how you used graphics and music, but the writing itself made it hard to fully understand the point being made. I clicked too fast my first playthrough and chose an option without reading it, but it felt like the conversations weren't really connected. The ending showed a bunch of squares being marked off, but I didn't know how or why those squares were marked so I just played a few times and tried picking choices randomly and it seemed to fill out the squares. But I wish the game had shared a bit more of the reasoning behind why those squares were marked off and what it was all about. Overall, a cool presentation but I think it just doesn't fit this jam.
Trick or Treat by
@ISC
Spoiler
This game was technically impressive, but unfortunately didn't fit the jam's main theme of a haunted building. Being inside while playing a card game with cute girls on each card just didn't feel spooky to me. There was a lot going on in the game but for the most part it made sense, though I did mostly choose cards based on what candies I had instead of trying to make the most out of the cards' powers.
I did have a lot of trouble with the game's RNG, as I kept getting stuck needing a certain candy to use any of my cards and not getting that candy at all from the candy bag. I know that I could just buy the candy (and I did end up just buying what I needed by the end of the game), but it felt like the game was really pushing me to ignore the candy bag completely which I don't think was the point. I also used a few cards that didn't seem to do anything obvious, I would click on them and then the cards would flicker but nothing seemed to change with either the opponent's mood or the candy count. I ended up with a total score of 998, which I'm guessing is low but with no comments from the game I can't be sure. Overall, it's very impressive that you made a card game in rpg maker but I think a different idea would have worked better in this jam.
Midnight Central by
@Rubescen
Spoiler
As someone who has missed her stop because she fell asleep, the setup definitely felt scary to me! The art was nice for the most part (I do wish you had left the faces out completely since they didn't match the cool art of the rest of the game), but the characters were a bit too cute and sweet to keep the spooky mood going. I did like all the characters though, they all had fun personalities so I was happy when I got to talk to them more and they'd say something new.
I think a major weak point of this game was how few hints were available. Most of the puzzles made sense, like needing the scissors to cut something or getting oil from the snake oil salesman, but a few like finding the flame for the lantern weren't as clear. I also almost didn't finish the game because I couldn't find the soul coins, I tried interacting with the skeletons from their feet and there was no message, so I didn't realize that their eyes were the coins. I think if there had been a visual showing what soul coins looked like or if those coin sprites sparkled a bit I would have realized that there was something special about them. Overall, this was put together well but I feel like there was a lot of backtracking and some of the puzzles weren't intuitive.
THE SYMMETRY -of Remorse and Penance- by
@werzaque
Spoiler
I'm willing to accept a spaceship as a haunted building, but I did feel like this game was missing spookiness due to its combat-heavy nature. The mystery was intriguing but my terrible luck made it impossible for me to finish the game since the fight with the four ghasts in the reactor room kept killing me. The combat was a lot more detailed than I was expecting with so many skills to choose from, but since I didn't have a lot of time to spend playing I did end up choosing one or two skills that seemed to do decent damage and sticking with them. Instead of everyone having 5+ skills I would have preferred something more like 3 skills that can be used to make combos with each other for higher damage. The enemies also could take a lot of damage, so I kept forgetting I should be a bit scared of the ghost ship since I was spending so much time trying to defeat foes. The unconscious memory world also felt out of place, it took me fully out of the haunted building and had me feeling like I was playing a normal sci-fi rpg... Which isn't a bad thing most of the time, but for this jam was a mistake.
You have a lot of details about this game world that you want to share, but I think the story was a bit too full for this jam. Overall I really enjoyed the concept and graphics, but felt like the combat and story could have used some shrinking down and simplifying to make it a more self-contained game.
Mystery Job by
@LunarSpire_
Spoiler
I'm not sure what to make of this game, focusing on an office building is a neat idea but the haunted part of the theme didn't come through. The Numan had a creepy design, but for the most part the game wasn't spooky beyond seemingly random jumpscares that caused game overs. There were so many bars that must have affected things but I couldn't find any rhyme or reason to why many of them changed. The Stench bar would jump up a bunch when I'd pick up normal meat, then drop when I picked up rotten meat, and then jump back up to almost full when I'd put rotten meat in the furnace, so I just couldn't figure out how or why it changed. I also fed the Numan a bunch of meat when it was hungry so it's bar was good, and then before I could even move it tried to jumpscare me so I was just left confused.
I only went down to the generator once, and was disappointed to find that it was powered by a math problem since that just felt like it was out of nowhere. I would have preferred if the generator was powered either by meat or made a bunch of noise that could draw the monsters' attention to me. The randomness in meat and rotten meat placement also gave me trouble, most of my attempts were filled with rotten meat so it was hard to keep the Numan fed even though I was really trying to find good meat... Overall, a really unique game in rpg maker but I think it could have used some cutting down of mechanics or more explanations to really help players know what's going on.
Nelly Come Back by
@alice_gristle
Spoiler
A short maze game that worked quite well. The graphics were cute and made it easy to tell what was going on, though the audio was so low that I could barely hear it. The story was limited, but I think that worked well for this. I did have some issues with the candle passability, I felt like I should have been able to get closer to their bases than I actually could so I almost got caught by enemies just because of that a few times. My biggest issue was the enemy pathfinding, the ones who 'chased' me often ended up lost or stuck so they weren't a problem to dodge. And the ones who could pass through walls tended to just float around blocking my path so I would need to just stand still for a bit until they moved and I could squeeze by. Overall, I think the game worked well and knew what it was aiming to do, I just wish the enemy pathfinding was a bit smarter to make me worry more while avoiding them.
The Dentist by
@r66r
Spoiler
A very unique concept, though I do admit that I don't find clowns or dentists all that spooky. The rules of the game were quickly explained which I appreciated, but I think you could have taken a bit more time to explain the differences between enemies. I thought the green-haired clowns couldn't be touched at all for quite a while, when they really were there just to block paths. And when I ran into the mid-size clowns they could just keep hitting me until I had run out of damaged teeth, which I didn't realize would happen since the enemies weren't explained. The tile passability was also a bit odd for a lot of the shelves, I get that you wanted to limit the paths but I kept getting caught on tiles that to me looked like I should be able to walk on and that would cause a clown to catch me. The size of the maze felt big, I get that you were using shopping carts to block paths but since they have wheels I was just confused why the kid couldn't move them. It felt like having a few different maps each with their own shop and clown could have worked better and gotten rid of a lot of the extra objects to block hallways.
I did get a game over my first try, but decided to give it another go since by then I understood the rules. I was pretty concerned at the ending, the poor kid was punched in the face by his mother for having one cavity and one broken tooth?! Overall, the haunted building was there but I think a shorter and more focused maze could have added more spookiness to the game.
Tuckamore Eve by
@BobbyLily
Spoiler
Snarky teens entering an abandoned house is always a good setup for a spooky game. I liked the custom art and the writing, though I do wish there was a bit more response to some of the stranger stuff like the family video playing in the basement or the crib filled with roots. The characters just felt a bit too blase about the whole situation. The root person silently appearing after picking up the ax got a genuine 'oh!' from me, which works way better to me than jumpscares, and I wish there were some more of those moments scattered throughout the game. I also couldn't find Note 3, was that tucked away somewhere that I missed or was that the one next to the basement key that couldn't be picked up?
I did play to get all four endings, and while I appreciated that each choice with the monster lead to a slightly different cutscene I wish there had been more to it besides picking one of four choices. Overall I enjoyed this game and just wish the ending didn't feel quite so rushed since it did drag the rest of the experience down.
Elysian Fields by
@ATT_Turan
Spoiler
A fun take on the haunted building theme. I do wish the youtuber-type setup played a larger part in the whole story, but it did set the scene well in the intro (and good use of creepy tiles and tints). I enjoyed the combat and liked that you chose creepy enemy designs, but it did feel a bit too easy once I realized that aiming for the enemy feet and then a head shot would take them out pretty quickly. I kinda wish that each character had their own focus for skills instead of them only being renamed, like Eve was the only one with head shot since she has the gun while the guys are much better at doing big damage to the limbs. But since I only had a few fights before the boss it wasn't a major issue.
The skill descriptions were set in such a way that they went out the side of the window, so while I could figure out what was happening it would have been nice to be able to read them fully before using the skills. I also wanted a few more conversations or quips from the team after fighting the normal enemies, since it felt like they weren't all that freaked out about the whole situation. Overall, a neat combat-based game that had some creepiness but could have used a few more scares.
NectaReal by
@karusomine
Spoiler
I enjoyed the intro of this game, kids going into a spooky house definitely offers a lot of possibilities. The art was nice and I liked the use of tints (though be careful when making the screen dark, it can be hard on some players' eyes!) and tileset choices, though the house's yard was really huge and could have been shrunk down a bunch and still kept the same spooky feel.
The gameplay is one of the weakest parts of the game unfortunately. I saw that you posted a guide to beating the Spider King, but I don't think finding the right path in the kitchen was the problem. I kept getting killed by the spider before getting anywhere near the kitchen, even when I tried booking it straight there. I tried to dodge, got killed. I tried running without stopping, I got killed. The one time I made it past the spider I had followed the same path as before, but for some reason the spider didn't kill me so I felt like it was random chance... Overall, the setup worked great but the actual gameplay really hurt the experience.
Ghost Puncher by
@Prescott
Spoiler
Fighting a whole ghost house floor plan was not what I expected, but it was a fun surprise! I liked that you tried to add voice acting, though I did skip through most of it since I read faster than the voices could speak. The house maps were nice to look at and not too big, so I never had an issue locating the ghosts. I did wish the ghosts were a bit harder to locate, like their possessed objects had a shimmer instead of the big circle icon, and there were more things to interact with, but I'm sure time was an issue.
Battles were the weakest part of this game unfortunately. Starting with so much money meant that I was able to stock up with 50 healing items each, so I went into the fights unconcerned. I also felt that the upbeat battle music really took away from the spookiness, I forgot I was fighting ghosts until they would use their Ectoplasm attack since I was just spamming the ultimate skill to beat them all. If the skills built up, so you needed to use the weaker ones to unlock the ultimate skill I would've had to think more about what to do each turn. The final fight was difficult but only because the enemy had so much health. I ended up with a score of 2829, which is good? Bad? I don't know but it's what I got. Overall, an interesting take on a haunted building but I think the combat needed some more work to make it more enjoyable.
SPOOKY JAAAAM by
@Jokokit123
Spoiler
Here is my 5k word essay about this entry:
Spoiler
Just kidding.
You ran out of time and it's unfortunate you were too sick to make the game, but the description did intrigue me so if you feel like making it into a full game go for it!
The Abby House by
@Izzy_MS
Spoiler
This game definitely nailed the 'haunted building' requirement with a house full of ghosts! I do wish you had used some more blue/purple-tinged screen tints and less upbeat music inside the house to add to a spooky atmosphere though, it was just missing a bit of creepiness to make me feel worried for Harold. I do like puzzles but I think the jumping puzzle in the backyard felt a bit out of place, especially after I tried to get haunted by being caught a bunch and realizing that the only thing that happened was having to restart... While making a puzzle too challenging is bad it would have been nice if there was more of a reason for why those ghosts were patrolling there and a consequence for failing to avoid them.
I'm not sure if you meant for the diary to be not in English. My Spanish is pretty rusty so I could only understand a few things which was a shame since it felt like a lot of the house's backstory was in that cutscene. The ending was very cute, and while I wish I could've seen the two of them dancing the eventing worked well enough. Overall, a nice little game that I think could have used a few more creepy moments to really make it seem like Lucius was worried about Harold vanishing.
President Evil by
@patedod266
Spoiler
Having to go into a creepy mansion to rescue people is a good setup, but I do wish there was a bit more to the intro than that mission picture that quickly disappeared. It would have been better if players had control of when that picture was erased, since I wasn't able to fully read it the first time I started the game. I liked the tiles you used, but a bunch of the rooms felt way bigger than they needed to be, especially since there weren't any enemies I needed to dodge in most of them. The lack of music throughout most of the game was also a miss, since you could have really made the place feel eerie with the right tunes. My intuition was really on point while playing so I kept going to the right door in the right order, so I didn't have any issues of running into locked doors and found my way around relatively easily.
Combat was the weakest point to me. Having gun skills tied to the number of bullets you have does make sense, but without an easy way to see if you have bullets in the skill menu it meant that I would try to use the gun and then do no damage. It may have worked better if you either had the bullets listed in the skill description, or tied the bullets to each character's MP since everyone seemed to mostly have their own types of ammo. Another thing is that the Reviving Pill can't be used outside of battle, so if I beat an enemy but one character dies I'm stuck with them being dead until then next fight starts (you can also use the pill on living party members, which pretty much is just throwing it away). Overall, this is an interesting take on the theme but I think smaller maps and more focus on either solving the mystery of the mansion or on combat would have lead to a more enjoyable game.
Pumpkin Decorating by
@slimmmeiske2
Spoiler
I'm always a fan of games where I can decorate and try different things, so taking the haunted building prompt and using it as a backdrop to a halloween party was clever. I played a few times to see what happened with different decorations, and it was nice that there were some dialogue changes but I wish there were some more blatant changes like using all candles leads to Reid starting a fire that the others needed to put out or Reid almost poisoning himself with an apple (really, just have Reid make poor choices when dangerous items are around). I only saw that the guests would say they liked the decorations or thought it was a bit lazy, so as long as I had some different things scattered around it didn't seem to make a bit difference. Overall, very cute and it was fun to decorate a few different ways, but I wish there had been some more comments or problems when using some of the decorations that Pumpkin warns about.
Slice of Dead by
@Wifi
Spoiler
I like the idea of the haunted building being haunted by monsters on purpose, but I think taking more time editing the dialogue could have improved this game a lot. The setup took a while and I wish there were more tints and effects used when showing humans being scared by the monsters. I was also confused when I was given control and told to go find the ingredients that are listed in the bag, but there wasn't any item that told me what to get. So I ended up just wandering around each room looking for any sparkles...
The music choices were also confusing to me. The normal exploration tune was really quiet so I had to turn my sound up to hear it and then was blasted by the overly loud default battle theme, completely taking me out of the spooky mood! I had to turn the audio off completely after that, so I may have missed any extra sound spooks. Overall, an interesting concept but needed more time to really bring it all together.

posts.body: Thanks! I entirely own the skill descriptions overflowing and janky tiles you pointed out to me - I succeeded too hard on my procrastination and didn't allow sufficient time to playtest a ton

posts.author: karusomine
posts.body: The spider was a real menace, huh. It's kinda funny in a way lol. Thank you for the feedback!

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
r66r
posts.body:
Thanks
@hiddenone
for the precious feedback. Apart from the lack of explanation of the gameplay, I found it interesting to know that the very design of the maze could pose problems... So getting feedback from experienced players or other RM games devs is really great, and that's why the jams here are so cool.
PS. The black eye isn't Mom's, but the result of one of the zombie punks who hit the kid.

Overall I enjoyed this game and just wish the ending didn't feel quite so rushed since it did drag the rest of the experience down.

Hit the nail on the head with this, the ending was absolutely rushed and I feel a good chunk of the game's shortcoming's would've been avoided if I wasn't rushing things so much.

That spider was the true terror of the mansion! I'm glad I was able to get past it to see the end of the game, I wasn't sure there after a couple game overs in a row.
werzaque said:
regarding the reactor fight, one can sneak past the ghasts to switch off the reactor but I think a hint wouldn’t have hurt.
Click to expand...
I didn't realize that. I did get past them at one point but I must've misclicked when exploring over there since nothing seemed to happen. That would make things a lot easier to finish.
r66r said:
PS. The black eye isn't Mom's, but the result of one of the zombie punks who hit the kid.
Click to expand...
So glad to hear that! I didn't pick up on that during the game, I saw that the zombie punks hit the kid's mouth but I didn't think about them also hitting the rest of his face. While it's a little silly to have the punks say what they're doing, it may be good to add a "enjoy that black eye, candy stealer!" comment or something.
BobbyLily said:
a good chunk of the game's shortcoming's would've been avoided if I wasn't rushing things so much.
Click to expand...
I was really happy to see the small changes between the endings that you did have time for, so you didn't totally run out of time. Finishing a game for a game jam is really tough and it takes a lot of practice and work to know what you can complete by the deadline, so don't feel bad about having to rush.

While it's a little silly to have the punks say what they're doing, it may be good to add a "enjoy that black eye, candy stealer!" comment or something.
Click to expand...
This is a typical case where the logic of the developer, who knows all the finalities of his game, is completely overturned by that of the player, who only has a vision of the part of the game he is playing.
Thanks for pointing this out... it's indeed a recurrent oversight to put oneself in the player's shoes when developing a game (even for a jam).

The Numan had a creepy design, but for the most part the game wasn't spooky beyond seemingly random jumpscares that caused game overs. The Stench bar would jump up a bunch when I'd pick up normal meat, then drop when I picked up rotten meat, and then jump back up to almost full when I'd put rotten meat in the furnace, so I just couldn't figure out how or why it changed. I also fed the Numan a bunch of meat when it was hungry so it's bar was good, and then before I could even move it tried to jumpscare me so I was just left confused.
I only went down to the generator once, and was disappointed to find that it was powered by a math problem since that just felt like it was out of nowhere. I would have preferred if the generator was powered either by meat or made a bunch of noise that could draw the monsters' attention to me. The randomness in meat and rotten meat placement also gave me trouble, most of my attempts were filled with rotten meat so it was hard to keep the Numan fed even though I was really trying to find good meat... Overall, a really unique game in rpg maker but I think it could have used some cutting down of mechanics or more explanations to really help players know what's going on.
Nelly Come Back by
@alice_gristle
Spoiler
A short maze game that worked quite well. The graphics were cute and made it easy to tell what was going on, though the audio was so low that I could barely hear it. The story was limited, but I think that worked well for this. I did have some issues with the candle passability, I felt like I should have been able to get closer to their bases than I actually could so I almost got caught by enemies just because of that a few times. My biggest issue was the enemy pathfinding, the ones who 'chased' me often ended up lost or stuck so they weren't a problem to dodge. And the ones who could pass through walls tended to just float around blocking my path so I would need to just stand still for a bit until they moved and I could squeeze by. Overall, I think the game worked well and knew what it was aiming to do, I just wish the enemy pathfinding was a bit smarter to make me worry more while avoiding them.
The Dentist by
@r66r
Spoiler
A very unique concept, though I do admit that I don't find clowns or dentists all that spooky. The rules of the game were quickly explained which I appreciated, but I think you could have taken a bit more time to explain the differences between enemies. I thought the green-haired clowns couldn't be touched at all for quite a while, when they really were there just to block paths. And when I ran into the mid-size clowns they could just keep hitting me until I had run out of damaged teeth, which I didn't realize would happen since the enemies weren't explained. The tile passability was also a bit odd for a lot of the shelves, I get that you wanted to limit the paths but I kept getting caught on tiles that to me looked like I should be able to walk on and that would cause a clown to catch me. The size of the maze felt big, I get that you were using shopping carts to block paths but since they have wheels I was just confused why the kid couldn't move them. It felt like having a few different maps each with their own shop and clown could have worked better and gotten rid of a lot of the extra objects to block hallways.
I did get a game over my first try, but decided to give it another go since by then I understood the rules. I was pretty concerned at the ending, the poor kid was punched in the face by his mother for having one cavity and one broken tooth?! Overall, the haunted building was there but I think a shorter and more focused maze could have added more spookiness to the game.
Tuckamore Eve by
@BobbyLily
Spoiler
Snarky teens entering an abandoned house is always a good setup for a spooky game. I liked the custom art and the writing, though I do wish there was a bit more response to some of the stranger stuff like the family video playing in the basement or the crib filled with roots. The characters just felt a bit too blase about the whole situation. The root person silently appearing after picking up the ax got a genuine 'oh!' from me, which works way better to me than jumpscares, and I wish there were some more of those moments scattered throughout the game. I also couldn't find Note 3, was that tucked away somewhere that I missed or was that the one next to the basement key that couldn't be picked up?
I did play to get all four endings, and while I appreciated that each choice with the monster lead to a slightly different cutscene I wish there had been more to it besides picking one of four choices. Overall I enjoyed this game and just wish the ending didn't feel quite so rushed since it did drag the rest of the experience down.

A fun take on the haunted building theme. I do wish the youtuber-type setup played a larger part in the whole story, but it did set the scene well in the intro (and good use of creepy tiles and tints). I enjoyed the combat and liked that you chose creepy enemy designs, but it did feel a bit too easy once I realized that aiming for the enemy feet and then a head shot would take them out pretty quickly. I kinda wish that each character had their own focus for skills instead of them only being renamed, like Eve was the only one with head shot since she has the gun while the guys are much better at doing big damage to the limbs. But since I only had a few fights before the boss it wasn't a major issue.
The skill descriptions were set in such a way that they went out the side of the window, so while I could figure out what was happening it would have been nice to be able to read them fully before using the skills. I also wanted a few more conversations or quips from the team after fighting the normal enemies, since it felt like they weren't all that freaked out about the whole situation. Overall, a neat combat-based game that had some creepiness but could have used a few more scares.

I enjoyed the intro of this game, kids going into a spooky house definitely offers a lot of possibilities. The art was nice and I liked the use of tints (though be careful when making the screen dark, it can be hard on some players' eyes!) and tileset choices, though the house's yard was really huge and could have been shrunk down a bunch and still kept the same spooky feel.
The gameplay is one of the weakest parts of the game unfortunately. I saw that you posted a guide to beating the Spider King, but I don't think finding the right path in the kitchen was the problem. I kept getting killed by the spider before getting anywhere near the kitchen, even when I tried booking it straight there. I tried to dodge, got killed. I tried running without stopping, I got killed. The one time I made it past the spider I had followed the same path as before, but for some reason the spider didn't kill me so I felt like it was random chance... Overall, the setup worked great but the actual gameplay really hurt the experience.
Ghost Puncher by
@Prescott
Spoiler
Fighting a whole ghost house floor plan was not what I expected, but it was a fun surprise! I liked that you tried to add voice acting, though I did skip through most of it since I read faster than the voices could speak. The house maps were nice to look at and not too big, so I never had an issue locating the ghosts. I did wish the ghosts were a bit harder to locate, like their possessed objects had a shimmer instead of the big circle icon, and there were more things to interact with, but I'm sure time was an issue.
Battles were the weakest part of this game unfortunately. Starting with so much money meant that I was able to stock up with 50 healing items each, so I went into the fights unconcerned. I also felt that the upbeat battle music really took away from the spookiness, I forgot I was fighting ghosts until they would use their Ectoplasm attack since I was just spamming the ultimate skill to beat them all. If the skills built up, so you needed to use the weaker ones to unlock the ultimate skill I would've had to think more about what to do each turn. The final fight was difficult but only because the enemy had so much health. I ended up with a score of 2829, which is good? Bad? I don't know but it's what I got. Overall, an interesting take on a haunted building but I think the combat needed some more work to make it more enjoyable.

This game definitely nailed the 'haunted building' requirement with a house full of ghosts! I do wish you had used some more blue/purple-tinged screen tints and less upbeat music inside the house to add to a spooky atmosphere though, it was just missing a bit of creepiness to make me feel worried for Harold. I do like puzzles but I think the jumping puzzle in the backyard felt a bit out of place, especially after I tried to get haunted by being caught a bunch and realizing that the only thing that happened was having to restart... President Evil by
@patedod266
Spoiler
Having to go into a creepy mansion to rescue people is a good setup, but I do wish there was a bit more to the intro than that mission picture that quickly disappeared. It would have been better if players had control of when that picture was erased, since I wasn't able to fully read it the first time I started the game. I liked the tiles you used, but a bunch of the rooms felt way bigger than they needed to be, especially since there weren't any enemies I needed to dodge in most of them. The lack of music throughout most of the game was also a miss, since you could have really made the place feel eerie with the right tunes. My intuition was really on point while playing so I kept going to the right door in the right order, so I didn't have any issues of running into locked doors and found my way around relatively easily.
Combat was the weakest point to me. Having gun skills tied to the number of bullets you have does make sense, but without an easy way to see if you have bullets in the skill menu it meant that I would try to use the gun and then do no damage. It may have worked better if you either had the bullets listed in the skill description, or tied the bullets to each character's MP since everyone seemed to mostly have their own types of ammo. Another thing is that the Reviving Pill can't be used outside of battle, so if I beat an enemy but one character dies I'm stuck with them being dead until then next fight starts (you can also use the pill on living party members, which pretty much is just throwing it away). Overall, this is an interesting take on the theme but I think smaller maps and more focus on either solving the mystery of the mansion or on combat would have lead to a more enjoyable game.

I'm always a fan of games where I can decorate and try different things, so taking the haunted building prompt and using it as a backdrop to a halloween party was clever. I played a few times to see what happened with different decorations, and it was nice that there were some dialogue changes but I wish there were some more blatant changes like using all candles leads to Reid starting a fire that the others needed to put out or Reid almost poisoning himself with an apple (really, just have Reid make poor choices when dangerous items are around). I only saw that the guests would say they liked the decorations or thought it was a bit lazy, so as long as I had some different things scattered around it didn't seem to make a bit difference. Overall, very cute and it was fun to decorate a few different ways, but I wish there had been some more comments or problems when using some of the decorations that Pumpkin warns about.

I had to turn the audio off completely after that, so I may have missed any extra sound spooks. Overall, an interesting concept but needed more time to really bring it all together.

posts.author: ISC
posts.body:
@hiddenone
,
Thank you so much for your feedback. I totally agree—I didn’t manage to integrate the jam’s theme into the game as well as I’d hoped. At first, I had planned to add a bit of story between sessions, but I ran out of ideas along the way.
The jam gave me a chance to experiment with something I’ve wanted to try for a long time, and in the future, I plan to improve this project, taking all the feedback into account. I’d like to give the game a stronger personality, better skills, and even a deck-building system to allow players to create their own custom decks.
Thanks again for your feedback; it means a lot and helps me aim to keep improving myself!

posts.author: Rubescen
posts.body:
hiddenone said:
As someone who has missed her stop because she fell asleep, the setup definitely felt scary to me! The art was nice for the most part (I do wish you had left the faces out completely since they didn't match the cool art of the rest of the game), but the characters were a bit too cute and sweet to keep the spooky mood going. I did like all the characters though, they all had fun personalities so I was happy when I got to talk to them more and they'd say something new.
I think a major weak point of this game was how few hints were available. Most of the puzzles made sense, like needing the scissors to cut something or getting oil from the snake oil salesman, but a few like finding the flame for the lantern weren't as clear. I also almost didn't finish the game because I couldn't find the soul coins, I tried interacting with the skeletons from their feet and there was no message, so I didn't realize that their eyes were the coins. I think if there had been a visual showing what soul coins looked like or if those coin sprites sparkled a bit I would have realized that there was something special about them. Overall, this was put together well but I feel like there was a lot of backtracking and some of the puzzles weren't intuitive.
Click to expand...
Thanks for your detailed feedback! Glad you liked the characters! Good notes on the hints, a lot of the latter segments were definitely rushed and a bit shoehorned in! Also good note on the coins. There is a a sparkle on them, but it definitely could be made more obvious given how small they are.
I'd originally planned to do a bit more with the gameplay, to hopefully make it feel more exploratory and less like running back and forth, but alas time ran out. Had a lot of fun with this - thanks for making it happen!
